payload.title: [tenant-app-isolation-6] Orphaned-blob GC only sweeps the _default app — non-default apps' blobs leak forever
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING tenant-app-isolation-6 (medium/resource-leak, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/blobs/gc-job.ts
LINES: 155-225 (runOrphanedBlobGc), 170 (listAllOldestFirst no appId), 242-256 (deleteBlobConsistently no appId)

WHAT: runOrphanedBlobGc calls `store.blobs.listAllOldestFirst(tenantId)` and `deleteBlobConsistently` → `store.blobDerivatives.deleteForParent` / `store.blobs.deleteContent` / `store.blobs.deleteMetadata`, all WITHOUT an appId argument, so every call defaults to DEFAULT_APP_ID (blob-store.ts methods all `appId = DEFAULT_APP_ID`). The declared-ref scan (collectDeclaredReferencedBlobIds) likewise reads `_default` objects. The job context provides no appId (see finding tenant-app-isolation-2), so even a per-app blob.gc job operates only on `_default`.

IMPACT: In a multi-app deployment, orphaned blobs (and their bytes/derivatives) uploaded under any non-default app are never garbage-collected — unbounded storage growth for those apps. No cross-app deletion occurs (the GC stays within `_default`), so this is a leak/cost issue rather than a data-loss-of-other-apps issue. Single-app servers are unaffected.

SUGGESTED FIX: Thread appId through the blob GC: enqueue/run one GC pass per (tenant, app), pass appId to listAllOldestFirst, collectDeclaredReferencedBlobIds, and deleteBlobConsistently's store calls. Depends on giving the job handler its appId (finding tenant-app-isolation-2).
